.github/workflows/ci.yml.text:
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
  RUSTFLAGS: "-D warnings"

jobs:
  check:
    name: check (${{ matrix.os }})
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [macos-latest, ubuntu-latest]

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5

      # ADR-0001 puts the shell on Tauri, which links the system WebView. macOS
      # has it; Linux needs the GTK/WebKit development headers.
      #
      # `cmake` and `libclang-dev` are Phase 13's: `llama-cpp-sys-2` builds
      # llama.cpp through CMake and generates its bindings with bindgen, which
      # dlopens libclang. Neither is a runtime dependency of anything shipped.
      - name: Install Tauri's Linux dependencies
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
            libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev libgtk-3-dev libayatana-appindicator3-dev \
            librsvg2-dev libsoup-3.0-dev libjavascriptcoregtk-4.1-dev \
            cmake libclang-dev

      # Phase 13 links llama.cpp through CMake (task 13.17).
      #
      #   MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET      -> rustc and the linker
      #   CMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET   -> the CMake build of ggml
      #
      # `llama-cpp-sys-2` forwards CMAKE_* variables from the environment as -D
      # defines. Without the second, ggml compiles below 10.15 and fails on
      # `std::filesystem`. Both are also in the workspace `.cargo/config.toml`,
      # which covers a local build; this covers a runner whose environment the
      # config does not reach first. RUSTFLAGS is not the place for either:
      # rustc rejects clang's `-mmacosx-version-min`.
      - name: Set the macOS deployment target
        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
        run: |
          echo "MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=11.0" >> $GITHUB_ENV
          echo "CMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=11.0" >> $GITHUB_ENV

      - name: Install Rust
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          components: rustfmt, clippy

      # ADR-0003 builds SQLite from source, which dominates a cold build.
      - name: Cache cargo
        uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          shared-key: toolog

      # Phase 5.1 puts the window on TypeScript and Vite. The bundle is
      # embedded in the binary, so it is built before anything compiles it, and
      # `npm run build` type-checks first — a frontend that does not compile
      # must fail CI as loudly as a crate that does not.
      - name: Install Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: "22"
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: ui/package-lock.json

      - name: Build the window
        run: npm --prefix ui ci && npm --prefix ui run build

      - name: Frontend tests
        run: npm --prefix ui test

      - name: Format
        run: cargo fmt --all -- --check

      - name: Clippy
        run: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings

      - name: Test
        run: cargo test --workspace --all-targets

      # Task 13.19 reserved a build without inference as the fallback if the
      # universal build could not carry llama.cpp. It can — measured, and
      # recorded in the phase file — so the fallback is not taken. It is still
      # compiled here, because a fallback that does not build is not one, and
      # because it is what keeps the GGUF reader, the prompt and the verdict
      # schema free of the C++ they sit in front of.
      - name: The build without inference still builds
        run: cargo check -p toolog-llm --no-default-features --all-targets

      # The Rust/TypeScript boundary regenerates itself during the test run
      # (Phase 4.9). A diff here means someone changed a command or a type and
      # did not commit the bindings.
      - name: Generated bindings are committed
        run: git diff --exit-code -- ui/src/bindings.ts

  msrv:
    name: msrv
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
      - name: Install Tauri's Linux dependencies
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
            libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev libgtk-3-dev libayatana-appindicator3-dev \
            librsvg2-dev libsoup-3.0-dev libjavascriptcoregtk-4.1-dev \
            cmake libclang-dev
      - name: Install Rust (MSRV from Cargo.toml)
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@master
        with:
          toolchain: "1.95"
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          shared-key: msrv
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: "22"
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: ui/package-lock.json
      - run: npm --prefix ui ci && npm --prefix ui run build
      - run: cargo check --workspace --all-targets

.github/workflows/release.yml.text:
name: Release

# Tag-driven (task 8.4). Pushing `v1.2.3` builds, signs, notarizes and
# publishes; nothing else does. The version in the artifacts comes from
# Cargo.toml, and the job refuses to run if the tag disagrees with it — a
# release named after a version the binary does not report is worse than no
# release.
on:
  push:
    tags: ["v*"]
  # Buildable without publishing, so the packaging can be exercised on a branch
  # without burning a version number.
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: write

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
  # Pinned with the one in the justfile: a `.app` built here and a `.app` built
  # on a laptop must come from the same bundler.
  TAURI_CLI_VERSION: "2.11.4"

jobs:
  bundle:
    name: Universal bundle
    runs-on: macos-latest
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5

      - name: The tag and Cargo.toml agree
        id: version
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          version=$(awk '/^\[workspace\.package\]/{f=1} f && /^version = /{gsub(/[",]/,"",$3); print $3; exit}' Cargo.toml)
          echo "version=$version" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "Cargo.toml says $version"
          if [ "${GITHUB_REF_TYPE:-}" = "tag" ]; then
            tag="${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}"
            [ "$tag" = "$version" ] || {
              echo "::error::tag v$tag does not match Cargo.toml's $version"
              exit 1
            }
          fi

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: "22"
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: ui/package-lock.json

      # Phase 13 links llama.cpp through CMake (task 13.17).
      #
      #   MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET      -> rustc and the linker
      #   CMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET   -> the CMake build of ggml
      #
      # `llama-cpp-sys-2` forwards CMAKE_* variables from the environment as -D
      # defines. Without the second, ggml compiles below 10.15 and fails on
      # `std::filesystem`. Both are also in the workspace `.cargo/config.toml`,
      # which covers a local build; this covers a runner whose environment the
      # config does not reach first. RUSTFLAGS is not the place for either:
      # rustc rejects clang's `-mmacosx-version-min`.
      - name: Set the macOS deployment target
        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
        run: |
          echo "MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=11.0" >> $GITHUB_ENV
          echo "CMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=11.0" >> $GITHUB_ENV

      - name: Install Rust
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          targets: aarch64-apple-darwin,x86_64-apple-darwin

      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          shared-key: release

      - name: Install the pinned Tauri CLI
        run: cargo install tauri-cli --version "$TAURI_CLI_VERSION" --locked

      # The window is compiled into the binary, so it is built before anything
      # links it, and `npm run build` type-checks first.
      - name: Build the window
        run: npm --prefix ui ci && npm --prefix ui run build

      # ci.yml triggers on branches and pull requests, which a tag push does not
      # match — so without this a release could be cut from a tree whose tests
      # fail, and the artifact would be signed and notarized before anyone knew.
      # The bundle is built from this same checkout moments later.
      - name: Tests must pass before anything is signed
        run: |
          npm --prefix ui test
          cargo test --workspace --all-targets

      - name: Import the Developer ID certificate
        # Decoded into a throwaway keychain so `codesign` can reach the private
        # key, and deleted again in the cleanup step whatever happens.
        env:
          MACOS_CERT_P12_BASE64: ${{ secrets.MACOS_CERT_P12_BASE64 }}
          MACOS_CERT_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.MACOS_CERT_PASSWORD }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          KEYCHAIN=build.keychain-db
          KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD="$(openssl rand -hex 24)"
          CERT_PATH="${RUNNER_TEMP}/cert.p12"

          echo "$MACOS_CERT_P12_BASE64" | base64 --decode > "$CERT_PATH"

          security create-keychain -p "$KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD" "$KEYCHAIN"
          security set-keychain-settings -lut 21600 "$KEYCHAIN"
          security unlock-keychain -p "$KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD" "$KEYCHAIN"
          security import "$CERT_PATH" -k "$KEYCHAIN" -P "$MACOS_CERT_PASSWORD" \
            -T /usr/bin/codesign -T /usr/bin/security -T /usr/bin/xcrun
          security list-keychain -d user -s "$KEYCHAIN"
          security set-key-partition-list -S apple-tool:,apple: -s -k "$KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD" "$KEYCHAIN"

          echo "KEYCHAIN_PATH=$KEYCHAIN" >> $GITHUB_ENV
          echo "KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD=$KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD" >> $GITHUB_ENV
          echo "MACOS_CERT_PATH=$CERT_PATH" >> $GITHUB_ENV

      - name: Write the App Store Connect key
        env:
          APPLE_AUTH_KEY_P8_BASE64: ${{ secrets.APPLE_AUTH_KEY_P8_BASE64 }}
          APPLE_AUTH_KEY_ID: ${{ secrets.APPLE_AUTH_KEY_ID }}
          APPLE_AUTH_KEY_ISSUER_ID: ${{ secrets.APPLE_AUTH_KEY_ISSUER_ID }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ -z "$APPLE_AUTH_KEY_P8_BASE64" ] || [ -z "$APPLE_AUTH_KEY_ID" ] || [ -z "$APPLE_AUTH_KEY_ISSUER_ID" ]; then
            echo "::error::notarization needs APPLE_AUTH_KEY_P8_BASE64, APPLE_AUTH_KEY_ID and APPLE_AUTH_KEY_ISSUER_ID"
            exit 1
          fi
          KEY_DIR="${RUNNER_TEMP}/apple-auth-key"
          mkdir -p "$KEY_DIR"
          KEY_PATH="$KEY_DIR/AuthKey_${APPLE_AUTH_KEY_ID}.p8"
          echo "$APPLE_AUTH_KEY_P8_BASE64" | base64 --decode > "$KEY_PATH"
          chmod 600 "$KEY_PATH"
          # The names Tauri 2 reads for notarization.
          echo "APPLE_API_KEY_PATH=$KEY_PATH" >> $GITHUB_ENV
          echo "APPLE_API_KEY=$APPLE_AUTH_KEY_ID" >> $GITHUB_ENV
          echo "APPLE_API_ISSUER=$APPLE_AUTH_KEY_ISSUER_ID" >> $GITHUB_ENV

      - name: Bundle, signed
        env:
          APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY: ${{ secrets.APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY }}
          APPLE_API_KEY_PATH: ${{ env.APPLE_API_KEY_PATH }}
          APPLE_API_KEY: ${{ env.APPLE_API_KEY }}
          APPLE_API_ISSUER: ${{ env.APPLE_API_ISSUER }}
        run: cargo tauri build --target universal-apple-darwin

      - name: Notarize and staple the dmg
        # Tauri notarizes and staples the .app, but only *signs* the .dmg it
        # puts the app inside. A user downloads the .dmg, so the container has
        # to be notarized in its own right or the very first double-click is
        # the Gatekeeper warning this phase exists to avoid.
        env:
          APPLE_API_KEY_PATH: ${{ env.APPLE_API_KEY_PATH }}
          APPLE_API_KEY: ${{ env.APPLE_API_KEY }}
          APPLE_API_ISSUER: ${{ env.APPLE_API_ISSUER }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          shopt -s nullglob
          dmgs=(target/universal-apple-darwin/release/bundle/dmg/*.dmg)
          [ ${#dmgs[@]} -gt 0 ] || { echo "::error::no dmg was produced"; exit 1; }
          for dmg in "${dmgs[@]}"; do
            xcrun notarytool submit "$dmg" \
              --key "$APPLE_API_KEY_PATH" --key-id "$APPLE_API_KEY" \
              --issuer "$APPLE_API_ISSUER" --wait
            xcrun stapler staple "$dmg"
            xcrun stapler validate "$dmg"
          done

      - name: What a clean machine will see
        # The assertions that matter, run against the artifact rather than the
        # configuration. `spctl` here is the same question a first launch asks.
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          app=target/universal-apple-darwin/release/bundle/macos/toolog.app
          lipo -archs "$app/Contents/MacOS/toolog" | tee /dev/stderr | grep -q "x86_64" \
            || { echo "::error::not a universal binary"; exit 1; }
          codesign --verify --strict --deep --verbose=2 "$app"
          codesign -dv --verbose=4 "$app" 2>&1 | grep -q "flags=0x10000(runtime)" \
            || { echo "::error::the hardened runtime is not enabled"; exit 1; }
          # ADR-0008: the app asks for no entitlements. `[Dict]` with nothing
          # under it is what an empty entitlements dictionary prints as.
          ents=$(codesign -d --entitlements - "$app" 2>/dev/null | tail -n +2)
          [ "$(echo "$ents" | grep -c "<key>")" = "0" ] \
            || { echo "::error::the app is signed with entitlements: $ents"; exit 1; }
          spctl --assess --type execute --verbose=2 "$app"

      - name: Checksums
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cd target/universal-apple-darwin/release/bundle/dmg
          shasum -a 256 *.dmg > SHA256SUMS
          cat SHA256SUMS

      - name: Clean up the keychain
        if: always()
        run: |
          [ -n "${KEYCHAIN_PATH:-}" ] && security delete-keychain "$KEYCHAIN_PATH" || true
          security list-keychain -d user -s login.keychain-db
          rm -f "${MACOS_CERT_PATH:-}" "${APPLE_API_KEY_PATH:-}" || true

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: toolog-macos-universal
          path: |
            target/universal-apple-darwin/release/bundle/dmg/*.dmg
            target/universal-apple-darwin/release/bundle/dmg/SHA256SUMS
          if-no-files-found: error

  publish:
    name: Publish the release
    needs: bundle
    if: github.ref_type == 'tag'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: toolog-macos-universal
          path: dist

      - uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v2
        with:
          files: |
            dist/*.dmg
            dist/SHA256SUMS
          fail_on_unmatched_files: true
          generate_release_notes: true
          body: |
            ## Install

            ```
            brew install --cask zaghaghi/tap/toolog
            ```

            Or download the `.dmg` below. It is signed with a Developer ID and
            notarized by Apple, so it opens without a Gatekeeper warning.

            ## Verify what you downloaded

            ```
            shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS
            spctl --assess --type execute --verbose=2 /Applications/toolog.app
            ```

            ## What it does on your machine

            The receiver binds `127.0.0.1` only. There is no analytics, no crash
            reporting, no update check and no account — see
            [PRIVACY.md](https://github.com/zaghaghi/toolog/blob/main/PRIVACY.md).
            Removing it is one command: `toolog uninstall`, which puts
            `~/.claude/settings.json` back byte for byte and keeps your recorded
            history unless you ask for it to go.

Cargo.toml.text:
[workspace]
resolver = "3"
members = ["crates/*"]

[workspace.package]
version = "1.2.0"
edition = "2024"
rust-version = "1.95"
license = "MIT"
authors = ["Hamed Zaghaghi <hamed.zaghaghi@gmail.com>"]
repository = "https://github.com/zaghaghi/toolog"
homepage = "https://github.com/zaghaghi/toolog"
description = "A local audit trail for Claude Code tool calls"

# Versions pinned from crates.io at planning time. Members opt in individually
# with `dep.workspace = true`; declaring one here does not pull it into a build.
[workspace.dependencies]
# --- internal ---
toolog-core = { path = "crates/toolog-core" }
toolog-ingest = { path = "crates/toolog-ingest" }
toolog-otlp = { path = "crates/toolog-otlp" }
toolog-cli = { path = "crates/toolog-cli" }
toolog-llm = { path = "crates/toolog-llm" }

# --- storage (ADR-0003) ---
# `bundled` compiles SQLite from source: no system dependency, no version skew.
rusqlite = { version = "0.40.2", features = ["bundled", "hooks"] }
# No refinery: refinery-core 0.9.2 caps at rusqlite <=0.39, so it would force a
# downgrade or a second linked SQLite. Migrations are a hand-rolled
# `PRAGMA user_version` stepper instead — see toolog-core/src/migrations.rs.

# --- OTLP receiver (ADR-0005) ---
axum = "0.8.9"
tokio = { version = "1.53.1", features = ["rt-multi-thread", "macros", "sync", "fs", "signal"] }
# `gen-tonic-messages` gives the prost message types without the gRPC stack;
# `with-serde` makes the same types decode OTLP/JSON, so one crate serves both
# wire formats (verified against the JS exporter's int64-as-string encoding).
opentelemetry-proto = { version = "0.32.0", default-features = false, features = [
    "gen-tonic-messages",
    "logs",
    "with-serde",
] }
prost = "0.14.4"

# --- ingestion (ADR-0002) ---
notify = "8.2.0"
walkdir = "2.5.0"

# --- secret redaction (Phase 7.2) ---
# Already in the graph via `tauri-utils`, so this adds a direct dependency and
# no new compilation. Patterns are data a user can extend, which means they are
# compiled at runtime and must be able to fail without taking the process down.
regex = "1.13.1"

# --- risk rules as data (Phase 6.1) ---
# TOML rather than JSON, because this is a file users are meant to edit: literal
# strings need no backslash escaping, and comments survive.
toml = "0.9.8"

# --- serialization ---
serde = { version = "1.0.229", features = ["derive"] }
serde_json = { version = "1.0.151", features = ["preserve_order"] }

# --- errors, logging, time, paths ---
anyhow = "1.0.104"
thiserror = "2.0.20"
tracing = "0.1.44"
tracing-subscriber = { version = "0.3.23", features = ["env-filter"] }
# Rotating local log files (Phase 4.11). Local disk only — never a network sink.
tracing-appender = "0.2.5"
jiff = "0.2.35"
directories = "6.0.0"

# --- hashing: raw_event dedup and the Phase 7 integrity chain (ADR-0004) ---
sha2 = "0.11.0"
hex = "0.4.3"

# --- the local second opinion (Phase 13, ADR-0013) ---
# `default-features = false` drops `openmp`, which Apple's clang does not ship,
# and `android-shared-stdcxx`, which is not this platform. `common` is not
# optional: `LlamaSampler::grammar` is behind it, and the GBNF grammar is what
# stops the model emitting anything but the schema (task 13.10). `metal` is
# added per-target by toolog-llm, because it is a macOS framework.
#
# This is the one dependency in the workspace that builds C++. It does **not**
# bring a network stack: llama-cpp-sys-2 passes `-DLLAMA_CURL=OFF` to CMake, and
# because a C library is invisible to the egress test's manifest check, that is
# asserted against the built binary instead — `just verify-bundle` (task 13.4).
llama-cpp-2 = { version = "0.1.150", default-features = false, features = [
    "common",
    "sampler",
] }

# --- test-only ---
tempfile = "3.27.0"

# --- CLI ---
clap = { version = "4.6.6", features = ["derive"] }

# --- desktop shell (ADR-0001) ---
tauri = { version = "2.11.5", features = ["tray-icon", "image-png"] }
tauri-build = "2.6.3"
tauri-plugin-single-instance = "2.4.4"
tauri-plugin-notification = "2.4.0"
tauri-plugin-opener = "2.5.5"
# The one dialog the app opens: "save this export where?". No network, and the
# path it returns is the only place the process writes outside its own store.
tauri-plugin-dialog = "2.4.1"

# --- the Rust/TypeScript boundary (Phase 4.9) ---
# A plain dependency rather than a feature: every type that crosses the IPC
# boundary lives in these crates, and a feature flag would let a build exist in
# which the bindings cannot be generated at all.
ts-rs = "12.0.1"

[workspace.lints.rust]
unsafe_code = "forbid"
missing_debug_implementations = "warn"
unreachable_pub = "warn"

[workspace.lints.clippy]
all = { level = "warn", priority = -1 }
pedantic = { level = "warn", priority = -1 }
# Noisy for a workspace whose crates are named after their domain.
module_name_repetitions = "allow"
# Docs are in ADRs and phase files; per-fn error sections are not the house style.
missing_errors_doc = "allow"
missing_panics_doc = "allow"
# Fires on any CamelCase word. These doc comments are architectural prose full of
# proper nouns (LaunchAgent, OpenTelemetry, SQLCipher); backticking them all would
# read worse than the lint is worth.
doc_markdown = "allow"

[profile.release]
lto = "thin"
codegen-units = 1
strip = true
